cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Scream – give a long, loud, piercing cry, expressing extreme emotion or pain.

p.em: Example: The scary movie made her scream in terror.

cosy-blockquote.p: Jekyll – representing the good or moral side of a dual personality (from Jekyll and Hyde).

p.em: Example: He showed his gentle Jekyll side by helping the elderly lady.

cosy-blockquote.p: Hyde – representing the dark, wild, or destructive side of a dual personality.

p.em: Example: When he is angry, his aggressive Hyde personality takes over.

cosy-blockquote.p: Freak – a person, animal, or plant that is abnormal or highly unusual.

p.em: Example: The heavy snow in summer was a complete freak of nature.

cosy-blockquote.p: Toyed – moved or handled something idly; played with an idea or concept.

p.em: Example: She toyed with the idea of moving to Paris for a year.

cosy-blockquote.p: Freud – referring to Sigmund Freud, the father of psychoanalysis who analyzed internal conflicts.

p.em: Example: Dr. Freud analyzed the patient's dreams to understand their hidden fears.

cosy-blockquote.p: Split – divided into two or more parts, factions, or groups.

p.em: Example: She has a split personality, with one side being quiet and the other wild.

cosy-blockquote.p: Identity – the fact of being who or what a person or thing is.

p.em: Example: Studying abroad helped her discover her true personal identity.

cosy-blockquote.p: Combination – a joining or merging of different parts or qualities in which the component elements are individually distinct.

p.em: Example: This delicious dessert is a unique combination of sweet and salty flavors.

cosy-blockquote.p: Gloomy – feeling distressed, sad, or lacking in bright light.

p.em: Example: The gloomy autumn weather made him feel like staying in bed all day.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Share whether you agree or disagree with these statements and discuss them with your teacher:

ul.li: Incorrect: There is a big improvement of → Correct: There is a big improvement in my English ((Use 'in' after 'improvement' to express domain.))
Incorrect: It was a great relief of → Correct: It was a great relief to hear the news ((Use 'relief' + infinitive 'to hear'.))
Incorrect: She is in the choir since → Correct: She has been in the choir for three years ((Use present perfect + 'for' to show duration of state.))
